conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here because of chest pain and we’re concerned about alcohol withdrawal. How are you feeling right now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m okay, just tired. The chest pain’s better since I sat up. But my heart’s racing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your heart rate is high and irregular. The EKG shows atrial fibrillation. We think this might be related to alcohol withdrawal or infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A-fib? I’ve never had that before. Is it dangerous?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can be, especially with your heart history. But right now, we’re focused on stabilizing you. Your labs show no heart attack, which is good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had chest pain for two weeks. It goes to my arm and jaw. I didn’t take my heart meds—I don’t know why.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. You’ve had stents before, so staying on meds is crucial. We’ve restarted aspirin and lisinopril. But we’re holding beta blockers because of recent cocaine use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I only used cocaine two days ago. I said I never used it before, but… I might have.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s okay. We just need the full picture to keep you safe. Your alcohol level was high, and you’re showing signs of withdrawal—tremors, confusion. We gave you medication to help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I drink a lot—20 beers and a pint of vodka daily. I couldn’t stop after my girlfriend left.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That puts a lot of strain on your body. We’re giving you vitamins—thiamine, folic acid—to protect your brain and liver.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your chest X-ray doesn’t show pneumonia, but you were recently admitted for it and left early. You didn’t get antibiotics then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I left because they weren’t listening to my chest pain. But I still cough up green stuff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re treating you for possible pneumonia with antibiotics. But the bigger issue is your heart function. The echo shows your ejection fraction is down to 25–30%.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It was 35% before. Is that bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It means your heart isn’t pumping as well. We need to manage this long-term, but today, we’re focused on withdrawal and infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your heart rate has improved with fluids and withdrawal treatment. But you’re still in a-fib. We’d like to keep monitoring you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m feeling clearer now. But I want to go home. I understand the risks, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I have to be honest—leaving now is risky. Withdrawal can lead to seizures. Your heart and lungs need follow-up. But I’ll support your decision if you understand.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I get it. I just need to get out. I’ll take the pills.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We’re giving you a prescription for levofloxacin to finish the antibiotic course. And keep taking the aspirin, lisinopril, and vitamins.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my heart rhythm? Should I see my doctor?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, urgently. You need follow-up for a-fib, heart failure, and your stents. We’ll send records to your PCP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the drinking? I don’t know if I can stop.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the hardest part. But there are programs to help. Please consider reaching out. Your health depends on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll think about it. Thanks, doc.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Call 911 if chest pain returns or you feel worse. We’re here if you come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge instructions are ready. Please take the levofloxacin for 7 days and follow up within a week.
